info.title: Bosun API
info.description: Local API of the Bosun engine. Sign in with a session cookie (send the CSRF token on changes) or an API token (`Authorization: Bearer bosun_…`).

get.description: Which advisory database the passive scanner matches detected component versions against: the small built-in one or a loaded feed, with its sequence, date, size and the public keys that may sign a feed.

post.description: Load an offline advisory feed: the file as text and its detached Ed25519 signature (base64). It is accepted only when the signature verifies under a trusted key and its sequence is higher than the database in force; it then replaces the built-in advisories and, by default, every recorded flow is queued for the scanner again. Nothing is fetched from a third party. Needs the admin role; audited (refusals too).

400.description: Not a valid feed or signature

409.description: The sequence is not higher than the one in force

422.description: No trusted key, or the signature does not verify

delete.description: Drop the loaded feed and go back to the built-in advisories. Needs the admin role; audited.

put.description: Set the Ed25519 public keys (base64, 32 bytes each, at most 5) that may sign an advisory feed. An empty list means no feed can be loaded. Needs the admin role; audited.

get.description: The distinct endpoints (ids in paths replaced by {n}, {uuid} and {hex}) and parameters of one host across the history, with counts, status codes and example values. Reads the newest 5,000 requests of the host (?limit up to 20,000); `capped` says there were more. Needs the viewer role.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many of the newest requests to read

get.description: The audit log, newest first. Needs the admin role or above.

post.description: The authorisation matrix: replay recorded flows as each of the given accounts and as nobody, and compare each answer with the owner's. An account that gets the same answer and is neither the owner nor listed in allowed is a finding (broken access control; missing authentication for no login). Account headers are given inline or taken from a vault entry opened on the server. Every send goes through the scope gate. Up to 200 probes and 20 accounts. With save_issues each finding is also saved as an issue. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

Sign in with a username and password. Sets the session cookie, unless the account has a second factor: then the answer holds a `pending` token for `POST /auth/login/totp` and no cookie is set. No sign-in needed.

200.description: A session (cookie set), or `second_factor` and `pending` when the account has a second factor: no session exists until `POST /auth/login/totp`

post.description: Finish a sign-in that asked for a second factor: the `pending` token and a TOTP code (or an unused recovery code). Each code works once; wrong codes count against the sign-in limits (429 with Retry-After). No sign-in needed.

401.description: Wrong code, or the pending sign-in expired

post.description: End the current session. Needs the viewer role or above.

get.description: The signed-in user and the CSRF token for cookie sessions. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Change your own password. Needs the viewer role or above.

get.description: Single sign-on button details, if configured. No sign-in needed.

post.description: Exchange the single-use, 60-second login ticket of an embedded engine (`bosun serve --embedded`) for an admin session. Loopback only; the exchange is audited. No sign-in needed.

get.description: Your own second-factor state. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Turn the second factor on with the first valid code, and get ten one-time recovery codes (shown once). Audited. Needs the viewer role or above.

400.description: Wrong code, or no enrolment in progress

post.description: Turn your own second factor off. Needs a valid code or an unused recovery code. Audited. Needs the viewer role or above.

Make a TOTP secret for your account (base32 and an `otpauth://` URI). Nothing asks for a code until `POST /auth/totp/confirm` receives a valid one; enrolling again before that replaces the secret. 409 when a second factor is already on. Audited. Needs the viewer role or above.
Make a new set of ten recovery codes; the old ones stop working. Needs a valid code or an unused recovery code. Audited. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: Require a second factor of every password account (single sign-on accounts and the desktop ticket are not asked). Accounts without one can then only reach the pages that set it up. Audited. Needs the admin role.

post.description: Start a browser preconfigured for the proxy (loopback servers only). Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: The CA certificate's fingerprints and PEM. Needs the viewer role or above.
The CA certificate for download. Needs the viewer role or above.
The project's custom passive checks. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Add a custom passive check written in the YAML check language. The text is validated with the check loader (size and pattern limits, a `passive` section, an id that is not a built-in's); a new check applies to new traffic at once and to recorded traffic after a rescan. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

400.description: Not a valid check; the message says what is wrong

409.description: The id is taken, or the project holds the most checks

post.description: Check a custom check's YAML without storing it. Always 200: `valid` and, when false, `error`. Needs the tester role or above.

put.description: Replace a custom check's YAML (validated like a new one). Needs the tester role or above; audited.

delete.description: Delete a custom check. Issues it already found stay. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

patch.description: Switch a custom check on or off. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: The project's client certificates for mutual-TLS targets: host pattern, subject and expiry. Private keys are never returned. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Add a client certificate (PEM with certificate and key, or PKCS#12 in base64 with its password) for a host pattern; the proxy and every tool present it to that host. The key is sealed with the data key. Needs the admin role; audited as `clientcert.add`.

400.description: Not a usable certificate or host; the message says what is wrong

409.description: The host already has a certificate, or the project holds the most

delete.description: Remove a client certificate. Needs the admin role; audited as `clientcert.remove`.

post.description: Compare two inputs (up to 1 MiB each, base64) by word or by byte. Returns runs of equal, deleted and inserted bytes with their offsets. Very different large inputs are reported coarsely. Needs the viewer role.

get.description: The crawls of this run of the server, newest first, with live counts. Progress is also sent on the event stream (crawl_started, crawl_progress, crawl_done).

post.description: Start a spider crawl from one or more URLs: it follows links, frames, redirects, GET forms, robots.txt and sitemaps, up to a depth and a page limit. Every request goes through the scope gate (a link outside the scope is listed in out_of_scope, never requested) and is recorded as a flow with source crawler, so the pages appear in the history and site map. POST forms are sent only with submit_post_forms. Two crawls run at once. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: One crawl: its state, the pages found so far from index ?from on, and, once it has ended, forms, out-of-scope links, robots and sitemap findings.

post.description: The stop switch: no further request is sent. `stopped` is false when the crawl was not running. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

Run a chain of up to 16 decoders or encoders (URL, HTML, Base64, hex, gzip, deflate, brotli, zstd, JWT, Unicode escapes, hashes) on base64 input. Returns each step's output (the last in full); a failing step is reported and the steps before it are still returned. Input and each output are limited to 4 MiB. Needs the viewer role.
Guess and apply a chain of decoders (up to 16 layers). Plain text is returned with no steps. Needs the viewer role.

get.description: The discovery runs of this run of the server, newest first, with live counts.

post.description: Start content or parameter discovery (forced browsing). Mode paths tries a wordlist (and optional extensions) below a directory URL and probes the directories it finds; mode params tries parameter names on one page. Before probing, random names that cannot exist are requested to learn what not found looks like, so a site that answers 200 to everything gives no hits, and many hits with the same answer are dropped as a wildcard (counted in noise). Every request goes through the scope gate and the per-host rate limit; only hits are recorded as flows (source intruder). Two runs at once. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: One discovery run: its state and the hits found so far (once it has ended also the directories probed, the wildcard noise dropped and whether the request limit cut it short).

post.description: The stop switch: no further request is sent. `stopped` is false when the run was not running. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: WebSocket event stream. ?since=N&epoch=E resumes after event N of that engine run (see ProxyEvent). Needs the viewer role or above.
List recorded flows, newest first unless sorted. Needs the viewer role or above.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: id (default), time, method, host, path, status, size, duration or mime. Ties break on the id.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip, for paging a list sorted by something other than id.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A history query (docs/query-language.md), combined with the other filters by and. A mistake in it is a 400.

delete.description: Delete flows by id. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: Check a history query without running it: the recognised terms with their positions, and every mistake. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Add and remove tags on many flows in one step (tags compare without regard to case; a flow keeps at most 32). Answers how many flows changed. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: One flow without bodies. Needs the viewer role or above.

patch.description: Set tags and note. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: A cross-site request forgery proof of concept for the recorded request, as an HTML attachment to open in a test browser that is signed in to the target. Only a GET or POST with a form, JSON-object or multipart body can be reproduced; anything else is a 422 that says why. ?auto=1 submits on load. Needs the viewer role.

422.description: The request cannot be reproduced by a form

get.description: Comments, scripts, references and URLs in the response, and the parameters of the request, for finding what to test next. Scans up to 2 MiB of each body. Needs the viewer role.
WebSocket messages of an upgraded flow. Needs the viewer role or above.
A message body, streamed. Supports a single Range; ?decoded=1 undoes Content-Encoding (parts: request, response, original-request, original-response). Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Import request definitions from an OpenAPI or Swagger file, a GraphQL introspection result, a Postman collection, a HAR file, a list of URLs or a Burp XML export, and save them as Repeater tabs. The file is only parsed: nothing is sent, and a tab is sent later through the Repeater, which passes the scope gate. The one exception is a GraphQL import with introspection_url, which POSTs the introspection query to that endpoint through the same gate (an out-of-scope endpoint is refused with 403) and records the fetch as a Repeater flow. HAR and Burp responses are stored as flows (source import, nothing sent) only when store_responses is set. Files over 32 MiB, YAML aliases, XML entities and deeply nested input are refused. The reply lists the hosts the requests go to. The import is audited. Needs the tester role or above.

422.description: The file could not be imported

get.description: Interception settings. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: Change interception settings. Needs the tester role or above.

post.description: Forward everything held. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: Held messages. Needs the viewer role or above.
One held message. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Forward (optionally edited) or drop a held message. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: Which responses are held when response interception is on. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: Change which responses are held (audited). Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: The project's attacks, newest first, with live progress for running ones.

post.description: Start an attack: fill the marked positions of a request with payloads (sniper, battering ram, pitchfork or cluster bomb) and send every request through the scope gate (the target must be in scope; there is no out-of-scope setting), recorded as flows with source intruder. Results are stored in the project and sent on the event stream (intruder_result, intruder_state). Up to three attacks run at once. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

409.description: Too many attacks running or stored

get.description: One attack, with its request (position markers included) and the configuration it was started with.

delete.description: Delete an attack and its results (the flows it recorded stay in history). A running attack is a 409. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: An attack's results in request order, up to 5000 per page (?offset and ?limit).

post.description: The stop switch: no further request is sent and the ones in flight are dropped, at once. `stopped` is false when the attack was not running. (The kill switch, PUT /tools/stop, ends every attack too.) Needs the tester role or above; audited.

Check an attack without sending anything: the request's positions, the payload sets, the options and the grep rules are validated, and the number of requests and the first `limit` requests' payloads (default 10, at most 1000) come back. A problem is a 400 that says what. Needs the tester role or above.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many requests to list, 10 by default, 1000 at most.

get.description: Issues the passive scanner found in recorded traffic, newest sighting first, with the number of flows it has not read yet. Filter by status, severity, confidence, rule, host, evidence flow or text. Needs the viewer role or above.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text in the title, detail or path

get.description: The issues (same filters as the list) as a report file: format html (default), json, sarif, junit or markdown. Always an attachment with a CSP that lets nothing run. Secrets (cookies, tokens, passwords) are redacted unless redact=0, which needs the tester role and is audited. Needs the viewer role or above.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: html, json, sarif, junit or markdown

post.description: Queue every recorded flow for the scanner again (after a rule changed). Counts start over; statuses are kept. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: One issue with its evidence ranges and remediation. Needs the viewer role or above.

patch.description: Set an issue's status (new, confirmed or false_positive). Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: One issue prepared for GitHub, Jira or Linear: title, Markdown body, labels and the JSON body of the tracker's create-issue call, to copy or post by hand. Bosun makes no request to the tracker. Secrets are redacted unless redact=0. Needs the tester role; every export is audited.
Map Local, Map Remote and throttle rules, in the order they are tried. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: Replace the Map Local, Map Remote and throttle rules (audited). A Map Local directory must exist and a Map Remote target must pass the scope gate, or the whole list is refused with a 400 that names the rule. Needs the tester role or above, and the admin role when the list holds a Map Local rule (it serves files from this machine).

get.description: Requests kept for follow-up, newest first, each with its status, note and the flow's summary. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Keep requests in the Organizer (ones already there are left alone). Answers how many were new. Needs the tester role or above.

delete.description: Remove an item (the request stays in the history). Needs the tester role or above.

patch.description: Change an item's status and/or note. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: The projects in the projects folder, the one that is open, and recently opened names. Needs the viewer role or above.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

post.description: Create a project, and open it if asked. Needs the admin role or above; audited.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

post.description: Close the project: a temporary in-memory one opens in its place. Connected clients are told to reload. Needs the admin role or above; audited.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

post.description: Import a project file sent as the request body (application/octet-stream). The file is never opened as it is: it is checked, then its content is copied into a new project. Needs the admin role or above; audited.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

delete.description: Delete a project that is not open. Needs the admin role or above; audited.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

post.description: Save a copy of a project in the backups folder. Needs the admin role or above; audited.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

get.description: Download a consistent copy of a project (including the open one) as a file. Needs the admin role or above; audited.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

post.description: Switch to a project. Held intercept messages are dropped, interception starts off, and connected clients are told to reload. Needs the admin role or above; audited.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

post.description: Rename a project that is not open. Needs the admin role or above; audited.

409.description: Conflict (name taken, project locked or open)

get.description: Proxy settings and resource counters. Needs the viewer role or above.
The proxy settings that change live, and the names of those that need a restart. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: Change live proxy settings without a restart (audited). A setting that needs a restart is refused with 409. Needs the admin role.

get.description: The proxy listeners and their options (passwords are never returned). Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Start another proxy listener without a restart (audited). Needs the admin role.

put.description: Change a listener's options live (audited); an empty password keeps the current one. Only an added listener can move to another address. Needs the admin role.

delete.description: Stop an added listener (audited); connections it already accepted run to their end. Needs the admin role.

post.description: Send a raw request once or many times (sequentially, in parallel, or as an HTTP/2 single-packet batch). Every send passes the scope gate and is recorded as a flow with source repeater. A send that is refused or fails comes back as a result with an error, not as an HTTP error. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: Whether the Repeater may send out of scope.

put.description: Allow or refuse out-of-scope sends from the Repeater (audited; goes back to refuse when a project is opened). Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: The Repeater's tabs as saved in the open project (requests and options; responses are not stored).

put.description: Replace the Repeater's saved tabs (at most 500). Needs the tester role or above.

post.description: Open a WebSocket with a raw handshake, send frames exactly as described (any opcode, reserved bits, FIN and mask), listen for a while, then close. The handshake is recorded as a flow with source repeater and the frames as its messages. Passes the scope gate. A refused or failed connection comes back as a reply with an error. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: Match and replace rules. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: Replace the rules (audited). Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: The project's saved history filters. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: Replace the saved filters. Every query must be valid. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: The active checks the scanner has: id, what each looks for, and whether it is destructive (saves data in the target, so it runs only when named in the scan's checks).
The scans of this run of the server, newest first, with live progress (units finished of planned, requests, findings).

post.description: Start an active scan of the given requests: each query, form or JSON value, cookie and (by strength) the last path segment or a header is probed by the enabled checks (see scan_checks). Every request goes through the scope gate (a target outside the scope is listed in refused, never contacted), is rate limited by the gate and the scan's own delay, and is recorded as a flow with source scanner. Findings become issues. Two scans run at once. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: One scan: its state, progress, the findings so far and, once it has ended, the refused targets.

post.description: No request starts until the scan is resumed; requests in flight finish. `changed` is false when the scan had ended or was paused already. Needs the tester role or above; audited.
Continue a paused scan where it stopped. `changed` is false when it was not paused. Needs the tester role or above; audited.
The stop switch: no further request is sent. `changed` is false when the scan had ended. Needs the tester role or above; audited.

get.description: The target scope. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: Replace the target scope (audited). Needs the tester role or above.

post.description: Analyse how random a set of tokens is (20 to 10000, each up to 1024 characters): per-position character statistics, bit-level bias, FIPS 140-2 (monobit, poker, runs, long run) on blocks of 20000 bits, an entropy estimate, checks for repeats and counters, and a verdict (excellent, good, poor, not_random). The result is the export. Needs the viewer role.

Start collecting tokens: send a request up to 5000 times (one after another, with an optional pause) and take the token from a response header, a Set-Cookie cookie or a regular expression over the body. Every request passes the scope gate (scope, kill switch, per-host rate limit; a rate-limit refusal is waited out) through the Repeater's engine and is recorded as a flow with source repeater. At most two captures run at once. Poll /sequencer/capture/{id}. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: The progress of a capture and its tokens from index `from` on. Needs the viewer role.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Return tokens from this index on

post.description: The stop switch: the capture ends after the request in flight. Needs the tester role or above.
Create the first admin account with the code printed at startup. No sign-in needed.

get.description: Distinct hosts and paths seen. Needs the viewer role or above.
Server name, version and whether first-run setup is pending. No sign-in needed.
Your API tokens. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Create an API token; the secret is shown once. Needs the viewer role or above.

delete.description: Revoke one of your tokens. Needs the viewer role or above.

put.description: The kill switch for all tool traffic. Needs the tester role or above.

get.description: All users. Needs the admin role or above.

post.description: Create a user. Needs the admin role or above.

delete.description: Delete a user. Needs the admin role or above.

put.description: Change a user's role. Needs the admin role or above.

get.description: A user's sessions. Needs the admin role or above.

delete.description: End all of a user's sessions. Needs the admin role or above.
End one session. Needs the admin role or above.

get.description: A user's API tokens. Needs the admin role or above.

delete.description: Revoke a user's token. Needs the admin role or above.
Remove a user's second factor and recovery codes (a lost device) and end their sessions. Audited. Needs the admin role.

404.description: That user has no second factor

get.description: The vault's named secrets: id, name, kind, timestamps and a masked hint. The secret itself is never returned. Needs the viewer role or above.

post.description: Store a named secret, sealed with the data key. Needs the admin role; audited as `vault.create` (by name, never by value).

409.description: The name is taken, or the vault is full

delete.description: Delete an entry. Needs the admin role; audited as `vault.delete`.

patch.description: Rename an entry, change its kind or replace its secret (left out keeps it). Needs the admin role; audited as `vault.update`.

feed.description: The feed file, as text: exactly the bytes that were signed.

rescan.description: Queue every recorded flow for the scanner again, so the new advisories apply to recorded traffic (default true).

signature.description: The detached Ed25519 signature over those bytes, base64.

loaded_ms.description: When the feed was loaded (milliseconds), if one is.

source.description: `bundled` (the small database that ships with the program) or `feed`.

trusted_keys.description: Public keys (base64 Ed25519) that may sign a feed.

keys.description: Base64 Ed25519 public keys (32 bytes each), at most 5. An empty list means no feed can be loaded.

biased_bits.description: Bit positions off one half beyond chance, and how many bit positions there are.

bit_stream_len.description: Bits in the bit-level stream (capped at 160 000).

capacity_bits.description: What the same positions would carry if every character seen there were equally likely.

charset.description: The most common characters over all tokens (up to 64).

entropy_bits.description: Effective entropy of a token in bits, character level.

oneOf.description: None when there are fewer than 20 000 bits.

reasons.description: Why the verdict is what it is.

sequential_share.description: Share of consecutive tokens that are numbers 1 to 65 536 above the one before (0 when they are not numbers).

tokens.description: The tokens, one string each (20 to 10000, each up to 1024 characters).

config.description: The payload sets, options and grep rules it was started with.

request.description: The request with its position markers, base64.

skipped.description: Requests left out because a payload was skipped.

state.description: `running`, `completed`, `stopped`, `failed` or `interrupted` (the engine ended while it ran).

similarity_percent.description: How alike two bodies must be (0 to 100) for the answers to count as the same.

skipped.description: Why there are no comparisons (the owner's own request did not succeed).

path.description: The backup file, in the `backups` folder of the projects directory.

days_left.description: Whole days until expiry (negative once expired).

expiring.description: True when the CA expires within 30 days or already has.

not_after.description: Expiry, seconds since the Unix epoch.

permitted_domains.description: Domains a name-constrained CA is limited to; empty when unconstrained.

count.description: How many requests to send (1 to 5000).

request.description: The request to send each time, as written, base64 (up to 1 MiB).

source.description: Where the token is in each response.

oneOf.description: Every cookie the answer sets.
The first capture group of `pattern` on the body, sent as `header: {prefix}{value}`.
A response header, sent as `header: {prefix}{value}`.

CaptureSpec.description: What to keep from the login answer.

error.description: What is wrong, when it is not valid.

CheckView.description: A stored check with the fields read out of its YAML.

check_id.description: The `id` in the YAML: the rule name on the issues it finds.

severity.description: info, low, medium or high; empty when the stored text no longer loads.

host.description: Host pattern: `api.example.com`, or `*.example.com` for every name under it.

pem.description: A PEM file holding the certificate (and any chain) and the private key.

ClientCertMeta.description: What a list shows: no key material.

forms.description: The lists below are filled when the crawl has ended.

out_of_scope.description: Links outside the scope, or that the gate refused. Never requested.

truncated.description: The crawl ended at the page limit with links left over.

pages.description: Pages the crawl has finished with so far.

requests.description: Requests sent, robots and sitemaps included.

error.description: Why there is no answer, or why it is partial.

concurrency.description: Requests in flight at once (1 to 32, default 5).

delay_ms.description: The least time between two request starts, milliseconds (at most 60000).

follow_resources.description: Follow `script`, `img` and similar sources too (default true).

headers.description: Extra headers for every request, each `Name: value`.

max_depth.description: Links followed from a start URL (0 to 100, default 5).

respect_robots.description: Do not fetch what `robots.txt` disallows (default true).

oneOf.description: Sign in before the crawl and again whenever the session ends (vault entries may fill the login).

start.description: Where to begin: absolute `http` or `https` URLs (at least one).

submit_get_forms.description: Send `GET` forms with the values the page gives them (default true).

submit_post_forms.description: Send `POST` forms with their default values. Off by default: a form can change data.

use_sitemap.description: Read sitemaps and queue what they list (default true).

stopped.description: False when the crawl was not running.

external.description:
Opened by path from outside the projects directory (`bosun serve --project /path/x.bosun`): in use, but
not managed through this API.

temporary.description: An in-memory project that is gone when another is opened.

oneOf.description: Forward, optionally with an edited message.

ops.description: The steps to run, in order.

oneOf.description: Set when a step failed; the steps before it are still returned.

steps.description: One entry per step that ran.

a.description: The left side, base64 (up to 1 MiB).

b.description: The right side, base64 (up to 1 MiB).

DiffOp.description: A run of pieces. `a_start` and `b_start` are byte offsets into the two inputs.

len.description: Length in bytes (of `a` for equal and delete, of `b` for insert).

coarse.description: True when the inputs were too different or too large to compare piece by piece.

equal_bytes.description: Bytes that are the same / different, for a one-line summary.

directories.description: Directories probed, or the page (params). Filled when the run has ended.

noise.description: Hits left out because they came in a wildcard cluster.

truncated.description: The request limit ended the run with words left.

cluster.description: Hits with the same answer share a cluster number.

base.description: Paths: the directory to probe (`http://host/app/`). Params: the page whose parameters to find.

concurrency.description: Requests in flight at once (1 to 32, default 8).

delay_ms.description: The least time between two request starts, milliseconds (at most 60000).

extensions.description: Paths: also try each word with these endings, written without the dot (`php`, `bak`).

headers.description: Extra headers for every request, each `Name: value`.

max_depth.description: Paths: probe the directories found too, down to this depth (0 to 10, default 2).

max_requests.description: Most requests, the baselines included (10 to 200000, default 5000).

post.description: Params: send the names in a `POST` body instead of the query.

words.description: Names to try (at most 100000). Empty: the built-in list for the mode.

stopped.description: False when the run was not running.

params.description: The names of the parameters seen on this endpoint (at most 100).

path.description: The path without its query, with ids replaced: `/users/{n}`, `/files/{uuid}`, `/blob/{hex}`.

statuses.description: How often each response status came back (requests with no response are not listed).

findings.description: What the response holds: comments, scripts, links, forms, resources, URLs and quoted paths.

params.description: The parameters of the request: query, form body and JSON body.

truncated.description: The scanned body was longer than the scan limit (or the decoded body was cut).

undecoded.description: The response has a Content-Encoding Bosun cannot undo, so only the request side is reported.

Evidence.description: A highlighted byte range in the stored request or response (end exclusive).

ExpirySpec.description: When an answer means the session has ended (default: status 401, or a redirect to a `login` page).

offset.description: Byte offset into the text that was scanned.

runs.description: Run counts for lengths 1 to 6 and over, for zeros and for ones: all must be inside their ranges.

bits_tested.description: Bits that went into the tests.

blocks_passed.description: Blocks in which every test passed.

limit.description: The range that passes, as text.

value.description: The statistic (ones, poker X, total runs or the longest run).

response_truncated.description: The body was larger than the recording limit, so only the start of it is stored.

FlowMeta.description: A flow without its bodies: its summary, and each stored message's head and size.

response_encoding.description: The response's `Content-Encoding`, when it has one. `?decoded=1` on the body endpoint undoes it.

FlowOverview.description:
A flow without its bodies: summary, each message's header block and size. The bodies come from the
`/flows/{id}/{part}/body` endpoints, a piece at a time.

FlowSource.description:
Where a flow came from. Every tool that sends traffic records it with its own source so history can be
filtered and so nothing a tool sends is hidden from the user.

FlowSummary.description: A flow as listed in history: everything needed for the table, without bodies.

edited.description: The flow was edited in the intercept queue or by a match-and-replace rule.

error.description: Error text when no response arrived (connection refused, TLS failure, dropped by the user...).

started_ms.description: Unix time in milliseconds when the request was received.

ttfb_ms.description: Milliseconds from the request being received to the response head arriving.

GrepExtract.description: Pull a value out of the response: the first group of the regular expression, or the whole match without one.

GrepMatch.description: Mark a response as a match when this is found in it.

regex.description: A regular expression rather than plain text.

Greps.description: The grep rules of an attack.

capped.description: The host has more recorded requests than were read; the newest were.

base_url.description: The server or endpoint to use when the file has none: required for GraphQL, overrides an OpenAPI server.

content.description: The file's text (at most 32 MiB). Not needed with `introspection_url`.

dry_run.description: Parse and report, but save nothing.

introspection_url.description:
GraphQL only: fetch the introspection result live by POSTing the introspection query to this endpoint
URL (it is also the base URL). The request goes through the scope gate like any Repeater request; an
out-of-scope endpoint is refused. `content` is ignored.

store_responses.description: HAR and Burp: also store the recorded responses as flows (source `import`). Nothing is sent.

added.description: Requests saved as Repeater tabs (0 for a dry run).

dropped.description: Requests dropped by the per-import limit (2000).

hosts.description: The hosts (`host:port`) the requests go to, so the scope can be checked before anything is sent.

not_added.description: Requests left out because the Repeater already holds the most tabs it can.

requests.description: One line per request: method and URL.

responses_stored.description: Recorded responses stored as flows (0 unless `store_responses`).

raw.description: The message as HTTP/1.1-style text (base64 so binary bodies survive).

in_scope_only.description: Only hold in-scope traffic (on by default: intercepting every analytics beacon is useless).

timeout_secs.description: Forward a held message, unedited, after this many seconds (none: hold until decided).

flow_id.description: The flow that shows the issue (the first one it was seen in); `None` once that flow is deleted.

pending.description: Flows the scanner has not read yet.

rules.description: The rule ids the scanner has, for filters.

primary.description: The listener from the config file: its options change live, but it cannot be removed or moved.

ListenerInfo.description: A listener as the API shows it. The password is never part of it.

ListenerSpec.description:
One proxy listener and the options that belong to it. The first listener comes from the `proxy` section of the
config file; others are added while running. Everything here changes live (a new address means a new bind).

addr.description: Address to listen on, for example `127.0.0.1:8081`. Loopback unless `auth` or `allow_clients` is set.

allow_clients.description: Only these client networks may use this listener (empty: anyone who can reach it).

oneOf.description: Basic credentials clients must send as `Proxy-Authorization`. The password is never returned.

invisible.description: Accept origin-form requests (`GET /path` with a Host header) as if they were proxied.

max_connections.description:
At most this many connections open on this listener at once; more are closed at accept (existing ones keep
running). Unset: only the proxy-wide connection limit applies.

tls_passthrough.description: Hosts whose TLS this listener tunnels untouched (scope host pattern syntax).

LiveSettings.description: Settings that change while running, without a restart. Everything else in the `proxy` section needs one.

header_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a client may take to send a request's headers (applies to new connections).

http2.description: Offer HTTP/2 to clients over ALPN (applies to new connections).

max_buffered_response.description: Buffered responses (response intercept, body rules) larger than this fail.

max_connections.description: Most client connections at once, summed over all listeners.

max_request_body.description: Requests whose body is larger than this are refused with 413.

record_body_limit.description: Only this much of each body is recorded.

record_out_of_scope.description: Record traffic to hosts that are out of scope.

upstream_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for an upstream response head.

LoginReply.description: The answer to a password sign-in: a session, or a request for the second factor (no session yet).

url.description: Absolute `http` or `https` URL of the login endpoint.

MapRule.description: One rule as saved. The fields a kind does not use are ignored.

bytes_per_sec.description: Throttle: response bytes a second; 0 is unlimited.

directory.description: Map Local: the directory files are served from.

host.description: Host to match: `api.example.com`, `*.example.com` for every name under it, or empty for any host.

latency_ms.description: Throttle: milliseconds added before the request is sent.

path_prefix.description: Match requests whose path (without the query) starts with this. Empty matches every path.

target.description: Map Remote: the origin to send the request to, for example `https://staging.example.com:8443`.

match.description: Literal text, or a regex when `regex` is true. Empty (header rules only) means "add".

save_issues.description: Save each finding as an issue (rule `authz-matrix`) that points at the probe's recorded flow.

headers.description: Headers that make a request be this account.

allowed.description: Accounts that are meant to reach it too.

flow_id.description: A recorded flow, replayed as each account.

owner.description: The account the flow was recorded as (an identity name).

csrf.description: Present for cookie sessions: send it as `x-csrf-token` on changes.

Options.description: The resource pool and the sending options.

concurrency.description: Requests in flight at once (1 to 64). The gate's per-host rate limit still applies on top of this.

delay_ms.description: The least time between the starts of two requests, milliseconds, whatever the concurrency.

max_requests.description: Stop after this many requests (at most one million).

retries.description: How often a request that could not be sent or got no answer is tried again (0 to 10).

timeout_secs.description: The longest one request may take, seconds (1 to 300).

update_content_length.description: Rewrite `Content-Length` to match each request, which is almost always wanted when a payload changes the body.

OrganizerItem.description: A request kept in the Organizer, with the summary of the flow it points at.

endpoints.description: Distinct endpoints it appeared on (counted up to 100).

more_values.description: More distinct values than `values` holds: likely an identifier, a token or free text, not a flag.

PartInfo.description: The head of one stored message and how big it is, which is all the flow overview needs.

body_len.description: The body alone: `total_len` less the head.

revoke_tokens.description: Also end the user's API tokens (default true).

PayloadSet.description: A source and the processing for what it yields.

oneOf.description: These strings, in order.
`from` to `to` (inclusive) in steps of `step`; a negative step counts down.

min_digits.description: Pad with leading zeros to this many digits.

oneOf.description: Every string of `min_len` to `max_len` characters from `charset`.
`count` empty payloads: send the same request many times.
Each item as it is, in lower case, in upper case, capitalised and with its case swapped.

Calendar dates from `from` to `to` (inclusive, `YYYY-MM-DD`), every `step_days` days (negative counts down).
`format` uses `%Y`, `%m` and `%d` (default `%Y-%m-%d`).

Each item with every combination of the substitutions applied (`a` to `@`, `o` to `0`, ...). Each rule
replaces all of its character in the item; at most 8 rules apply to one item.
A small wordlist that ships with Bosun: `passwords`, `usernames`, `paths` or `numbers-0-99`.

index.description: The payloads of one request (one per position, or one for sniper and battering ram).

total.description: Requests the attack would make (after the maximum, before skipped payloads are left out).

biased_bits.description: How many of those bits are off one half by more than chance allows (|z| above 3.29).

bit_ones.description: For each of those bits (most significant first): the share of ones.

bits.description: Bits taken from this character for the bit-level analysis.

top_char.description: The most common character and its share.

oneOf.description: Encode, escape or hash with one of the Decoder's operations (URL, HTML, Base64, hex, SHA-256, ...).
Replace every match of the regular expression; `$1` in the replacement is the first group.
Leave out any payload that matches the regular expression.

Processing.description: A step applied to every payload, in order.

password_file.description: File holding the password (container secrets); read at start-up, and instead of `password`.

ProxyConfigView.description: The live settings, and the names of the settings that need a restart.

oneOf.description: A flow was written to history.
A message could not be held (queue full) and was refused.
A batch of history could not be written even after a retry, and is lost.

Another project is open now: everything a client holds (history, scope, rules, held messages) is from
the old one, so it should fetch it all again. `name` is empty for the temporary project.
The passive scanner found something, or caught up with the history: look at the issues again.
An Intruder attack started, moved on or ended.
A crawl was accepted and is running.
A running crawl has more pages (sent at most a few times a second). Fetch `/crawl/crawls/{id}?from=N`.
A crawl ended: `state` is `done`, `stopped` or `failed`.
An active scan was accepted and is running.
A running active scan moved on (sent at most four times a second). Fetch `/scan/scans/{id}`.
An active scan ended: `state` is `done`, `stopped` or `failed`.
One request of an Intruder attack finished. (The same fields as a stored result.)

ProxyEvent.description: Events the proxy publishes for front ends (sent over the API's event stream).

connections_refused.description: Connections closed at once because the proxy was at its connection limit.

QueryCheck.description:
What a history query means: each recognised term with its place in the text, and every mistake. Nothing is
run. A front end uses this for chips and messages while the person types.

allow_out_of_scope.description: Let the Repeater send to hosts outside the scope. Starts off, and goes back off when a project is opened.

ResponseFilter.description:
Which responses are held when response interception is on. Every condition that is set must match; an empty
filter holds every response.

body_contains.description: A substring that must appear in the response body (the body is buffered to check it).

header_contains.description: A substring that must appear in the response's header lines (case-insensitive).

mime_contains.description: Substrings of the `Content-Type` (any one may match, case-insensitive). Empty: any type.

only_if_request_held.description: Hold only responses whose request was held too.

statuses.description: Status codes or classes, such as `404`, `5xx` (any one may match). Empty: any status.

attempts.description: How many tries it took (1 when the first worked).

extracts.description: One entry per grep extract rule.

flow_id.description: The recorded flow, when something was sent.

matches.description: One entry per grep match rule.

payloads.description: The payloads used, as text (bytes that are not UTF-8 are replaced).

position.description: The position that was attacked, for a sniper attack.

SavedFilter.description: A history query kept under a name, for the whole project.

destructive.description: Saves data in the target application: off unless named in `checks`.

changed.description: False when the scan was not running (or, for resume, not paused).

refused.description: Targets the gate refused (outside the scope). Never contacted. Filled when the scan has ended.

truncated.description: The request cap ended the scan with work left.

flow_id.description: The flow that proves it; the issue list shows the finding too.

units_done.description: Units of work (a target and one insertion point) finished, and planned.

checks.description: Check ids (see scan_checks); empty runs every check that is not destructive, and a destructive one (it saves data in the target) runs only when named.

concurrency.description: Units of work in flight at once (1 to 32, default 4).

delay_ms.description: The least time between two request starts in one unit, milliseconds (at most 60000).

headers.description: Extra headers for every request, each `Name: value`.

max_requests.description: The most requests the scan may send (1 to 200000, default 5000).

oneOf.description: Sign in before the scan and again whenever the session ends (vault entries may fill the login).

strength.description: `low`, `medium` (default) or `high`: more insertion points and probes.

content_type.description:
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (default with a body) or `application/json`: their values are
insertion points.

headers.description: Each `Name: value`. A `Cookie` header makes its cookies insertion points.

url.description: Absolute `http` or `https` URL; its query values are insertion points.

ScopeRule.description: One include or exclude rule, as the user writes it.

allow_private.description:
Let this rule reach loopback, link-local and the host's own networks. Off by default, so a public name
that is made to resolve to `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254` is refused.

host.description:
Host glob, case-insensitive. `example.com` matches that host only; `*.example.com` matches one level of
sub-domain (`*` never crosses a dot), so add a rule per level you want. IP addresses work as literals.

path.description: Regex matched against the path (without the query), or empty for any path.

oneOf.description: `http`, `https`, or empty for both.

pending.description: Send this with the code to `POST /auth/login/totp`. Valid for five minutes, from the same address.

second_factor.description: The kind of second factor to present: `totp`.

count.description: How many times to send it (1 to 100).

follow_redirects.description: Follow redirects (HTTP/1.1 only), recording each hop.

update_content_length.description: Rewrite `Content-Length` to match the body. Off by default: what you wrote is what is sent.

error.description: Why there is no (or only a partial) response.

flow_id.description: The recorded flow, when something was sent.

h2_frames.description: Number of HTTP/2 frames written and read, when the exchange was HTTP/2.

hop.description: Which redirect hop (0 is the request itself).

index.description: Which of the `count` sends this is (0-based).

refused.description: The scope gate or the kill switch stopped it; nothing was sent.

reused.description: The connection came from the pool or was shared.

SessionInfo.description:
A signed-in browser session, as shown to its owner and to admins. The id is a prefix of the stored hash; it
cannot be used to sign in.

SiteMapEntry.description: A host and the paths seen on it, for the site map.

name.description: A label for the attack (defaults to the host and attack type).

payload_sets.description: One set for sniper and battering ram; one per position for pitchfork and cluster bomb.

request.description:
The request, base64, with `§` around each position (`§value§`: the text between is what is sent when the
position is not being attacked).

output.description: The output, base64: whole for the last step, up to 64 KiB for the others.

size.description: The step's full output size in bytes.

stopped.description: False when the attack was not running.

TabsDoc.description:
The Repeater's tabs as the page keeps them. The server stores them as the page wrote them and looks only at their
count and shape, so the page can add a field without a server change.

active.description: Id of the tab that was open.

next.description: The id the next new tab gets.

tabs.description: One object per tab (target, request text, options). Responses are not stored.

truncated.description: A limit was hit: there were more endpoints or parameters than are listed.

TermSpan.description: A recognised term, for showing as a chip: where it is in the query and what it says.

label.description: The term as written, including a leading `-`.

ticket.description: The single-use ticket an embedded engine printed for its parent.

TokenScope.description: What an API token may do. A `Read` token can only make requests that don't change anything (GET, HEAD).

oneOf.description: The value of a response header (the first with that name).
The value of a `Set-Cookie` cookie.
A regular expression over the body: capture group 1 if there is one, else the whole match.

TokenSource.description: Where a token sits in a response.

code.description: A 6-digit code (a recovery code also works where the operation allows it).

otpauth_uri.description: The same secret as an `otpauth://` URI.

secret.description: The shared secret, base32. Shown once.

code.description: A 6-digit code, or an unused recovery code.

enabled.description: A confirmed second factor is on for this account.

enrolling.description: A secret was made but no code has confirmed it yet.

required.description: An admin requires every password account to have a second factor.

setup_required.description: This account must set up a second factor before it can do anything else.

TrackerReply.description: What `GET /issues/{id}/tracker` returns: one issue prepared for an issue tracker.

payload.description: The JSON body for the tracker's create-issue call.

secret.description: The secret. Stored sealed; never returned.

VaultEntry.description: What a list shows: no secret.

hint.description: A masked hint such as `••••ab`; never enough to recover the secret.

VaultHeader.description: Where a header value comes from: a vault entry, opened on the server.

header.description: The header to set, such as `Authorization` or `Cookie`.

prefix.description: Text put before the secret, such as `Bearer `.

secret.description: A new secret; leave out to keep the current one.

frames.description: Frames to send, in order, once the server has answered `101`.

listen_ms.description: How long to keep listening after the last frame, in milliseconds (at most 10000).

request.description: The handshake, a raw HTTP/1.1 upgrade request, base64.

mask.description:
`random` (the default), `none` (send unmasked, which a compliant client never does) or four bytes as eight
hex digits.

opcode.description: 0 continuation, 1 text, 2 binary, 8 close, 9 ping, 10 pong; anything from 0 to 15 is sent as given.

rsv.description: The three reserved bits as a number from 0 to 7.

WsMessage.description: A WebSocket message seen on an upgraded connection.

flow_id.description: The flow holding the HTTP upgrade handshake.

closed_by_server.description: The server sent a close frame.

error.description: Why there is no open connection or why listening stopped early.

flow_id.description: The handshake as a recorded flow; the frames are its messages.

frames.description: Frames sent and received, in the order they happened (sent ones first, then what came back).

refused.description: The scope gate or the kill switch stopped it; nothing was sent.

request.description: The handshake request and the server's answer, base64.
